name: grep
description:
Regex search over file contents, fast on any repository size.

How it works:
- `pattern` is a regular expression (for example "log.*Error" or "function\s+\w+"); the full regex syntax is available.
- Each result is a file path with the line numbers that matched at least once.
- `include` limits the search to files matching a glob such as "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}", and `path` limits it to one directory.
- `repo` names the repository to search; if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first. Leave it out to search every repository. `ref` picks a branch, tag or commit (default branch otherwise).
- `limit` caps the number of matches.
- Set `groupByRepo: true` to see how matches spread over many repositories before you dig into one. It returns per-repository match and file counts instead of file results, and applies a higher limit so the counts are accurate.

pattern.description: Regular expression to look for inside files.

path.description: Only search this directory (default: the repository root).

include.description: Glob that file names must match, e.g. "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}".

repo.description: Repository to search. Omit to search all of them.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag to search (default: the default branch).

limit.description: Most matches to return (default 100, or 10000 when groupByRepo is true).

groupByRepo.description: When true, return match and file counts per repository rather than individual file results.

name: glob
description:
Lists file paths whose name or path matches a glob pattern. It never looks inside files; use `grep` for content.

How it works:
- `pattern` uses glob syntax: `*` stays within one path segment, `**` crosses segments, `{a,b}` offers alternatives (for example "**/*.ts" or "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}").
- `path` restricts matches to one subdirectory, `ref` picks a branch, tag or commit, and `limit` caps how many files come back.
- `repo` names the repository to search; if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first. Leave it out to search every repository.
- Reach for this when you want every file of some kind or naming convention.

pattern.description: Glob matched against file paths, e.g. "**/*.ts" or "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}".

path.description: Only return files below this subdirectory.

repo.description: Repository to search. Omit to search all of them.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag to search (default: the default branch).

name: get_diff
description:
Shows what changed between two git refs of a repository, as a structured diff.

Pass `repo`, a `base` ref and a `head` ref (each a branch, tag or commit SHA); add `path` to look at one file only. The result lists the changed files with their hunks: line ranges plus the added, removed and surrounding lines. Use it when you need the actual patch, not just the list of commits.

base.description: Ref (branch, tag or commit SHA) to compare from.

head.description: Ref (branch, tag or commit SHA) to compare to.

path.description: Only include changes to this file. Omit to include every change between the two refs.

name: list_commits
description:
Lists the commits of a repository, newest first, with optional filters.

Parameters:
- `repo`: the repository; if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first.
- `query`: match against commit messages (case-insensitive, substrings and simple patterns).
- `since` and `until`: bound the dates, as ISO 8601 ("2024-01-01") or relative text ("30 days ago", "last week", "yesterday").
- `author`: part of an author's name or email (case-insensitive).
- `path`: only commits that touched this file or directory. For a path under `knowledge-base/` the history lives in the repository's knowledge repository: the result's `repo` names it and `path` is relative to it, so use that pair for follow-up calls on those commits.
- `ref`: a branch, tag or commit SHA to list from (default branch otherwise).
- `page` and `perPage`: paging; compare the response's `totalCount` with what you have seen to know whether more pages exist.

query.description: Text to find in commit messages (case-insensitive).

since.description: Earliest date to include: an ISO date like '2024-01-01' or relative text like 'last week'.

until.description: Latest date to include: an ISO date like '2024-12-31' or relative text like 'yesterday'.

author.description: Part of an author's name or email (case-insensitive).

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag to list history of (default: the default branch).

path.description: Only commits touching this file or directory, relative to the repository root.

name: list_branches
description:
Lists the branches of a repository, most recently committed first.

Parameters and fields:
- `repo`: the repository; if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first.
- The data is Falkon's last fetch of the repository, not the live code host: a branch created or deleted there shows up here only after the next fetch.
- `query` keeps branches whose name contains the text (case-insensitive).
- `page` and `perPage` page through long lists; compare `totalCount` in the response with what you have seen to know whether more exist.
- `isDefault` flags the default branch. `isIndexed` says whether the branch can be searched with `grep` and `glob`; a branch with `isIndexed: false` exists but is not searchable.

query.description: Keep only branches whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

name: list_repos
description: Lists the repositories you can see, with optional name filter, sorting and paging. `query` filters by name, `sort` orders by name or latest push, `direction` flips the order, and `page` with `perPage` pages through the result.

query.description: Keep only repositories whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

sort.description: Order by 'name' or by 'pushed' (latest commit). Default 'name'.

name: read_file
description:
Returns the text of one file in a repository, with line numbers.

Parameters and limits:
- `repo` and `path` identify the file; `ref` picks a branch, tag or commit (default branch otherwise).
- `offset` (first line, 1-based) and `limit` (line count) select a slice. Prefer a slice over the whole file when you only need one section.
- One call returns at most 500 lines and about 5KB. If that cap cuts the output short, call again with a later `offset` to continue.
- Lines longer than 2000 characters are cut off.
- The response states the range it returned and the file's total line count, plus the next `offset` when it was truncated.
- Independent files can be read in parallel calls. Prefer one larger window over many tiny slices.

path.description: Path of the file inside the repository.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag to read the file at (default: the default branch).

offset.description: First line to return, 1-based. Omit to start at the top.

limit.description: Number of lines to return, at most 500. Omit for up to 500.

name: list_tree
description:
Lists the files and directories under a path of a repository, as flat entries with their path and depth below the requested path. Use it as a directory listing or a repository tree.

Parameters:
- `repo`: the repository; if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first.
- `path`: the directory to list, so you can look at one subtree instead of everything; `ref` picks a branch, tag or commit.
- `depth`: how many levels to descend (default 1). Start shallow for an overview, then go deeper into the directories that matter.
- `includeFiles: false` keeps only directories; `includeDirectories: false` keeps only files.
- `maxEntries` caps the number of entries.
- Exploring several directories? Make the calls in parallel.

path.description: Directory to list, relative to the repository root. Omit for the root.

ref.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag to list at (default: the default branch).

depth.description: Directory levels to descend below `path`, 1 to 10 (default 1).

name: find_symbol_definitions
description:
Locates where a named symbol (function, class, variable, method, type and so on) is defined.

How it works:
- Answers "where is X defined or implemented?".
- Give the exact identifier as `symbol` ("UserService", not "user service class"); `repo` limits the search to one repository, and if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first.
- The result lists each definition site as a file path with line numbers, grouped by file.
- Better than `grep` for this job: matching respects symbol boundaries, so partial words and comments do not show up.

symbol.description: Exact name of the symbol to find definitions of.

name: find_symbol_references
description:
Lists the places where a named symbol (function, class, variable, method, type and so on) is used.

How it works:
- Answers "where is X used or called?".
- Give the exact identifier as `symbol` ("getUserById", not "get user by id"); `repo` limits the search to one repository, and if you do not know its name, call `list_repos` first.
- The result lists each use as a file path with line numbers, grouped by file.
- Better than `grep` for this job: matching respects symbol boundaries, so partial words and comments do not show up.

symbol.description: Exact name of the symbol to find uses of.

name: list_language_models
description: Returns the language models this Falkon instance is configured with, so you can pick one for the languageModel parameter of ask_codebase.

name: ask_codebase
description:
Only call this tool when the user's request names ask_codebase explicitly; otherwise use the search and read tools yourself.

Puts a natural-language question about the code to a Falkon agent. The agent runs its own searches, reads files and follows symbol definitions and references, then writes the answer.

Pass the question as `query`; optionally narrow the agent with `repos` and choose a model with `languageModel` (see list_language_models).

The call blocks while the agent works and can take a minute or more.

Returns markdown with code references, followed by a link to the saved chat thread in the Falkon UI, where every tool call and step of the research can be reviewed.

For a chat shared with others (a Slack thread, say), pass visibility 'PUBLIC' so the link opens for everyone.

query.description: The query to ask about the codebase.

repos.description: Repositories the agent may search. Omit to let it use every repository you can see.

displayName.description: Optional display name for the model

inputModalities.description: The input modalities the model can accept (images, audio, video, text). Single-medium attachments are gated by these. Defaults to text-only.

supportedDocumentTypes.description: Rich compound document formats (e.g. PDF) the model can ingest natively, distinct from single-medium attachments gated by inputModalities. Defaults to none.

languageModel.description: Model that runs the agent. Omit to use the first configured model.

visibility.description: Who can open the saved chat. Defaults to PRIVATE for signed-in callers.

name: research_codebase
description: Prepare a repository-scoped research brief for your model to answer a code question with Falkon's search and read tools. Returns a workflow and citation guidance without calling a server model.

query.description: The question to investigate in source code.

repos.description: Repository names to select from your visible repositories. Omit for all visible repositories; an empty list selects none.
